output_units.source_text:
<STRUCT_0001>
The existence of finite covers of Deligne-Mumford stacks by schemes
is an important result. In intersection theory on Deligne-Mumford
stacks, it is an essential ingredient in defining proper push-forward
for non-representable morphisms. There are several
results about <MATH_0001> relying on the existence of a finite
cover by a <EMPHOPEN_0001>smooth<EMPHCLOSE_0001> scheme which was proven by Looijenga. Perhaps the
first result in this direction is <REF_0001>
which treats the equivariant setting.
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> Vistoli: <EMPHOPEN_0002>Intersection theory on algebraic stacks and on their
moduli spaces<EMPHCLOSE_0002> <REF_0002>
<STRUCT_0004>
If <MATH_0002> is a Deligne-Mumford stack with a moduli space (ie. a proper
morphism
which is bijective on geometric points), then there exists a finite morphism
<MATH_0003> from a scheme <MATH_0004>.
<STRUCT_0005>
<STRUCT_0006> Laumon, Moret-Bailly: <REF_0003>
<STRUCT_0007>
As an application of Zariski's main theorem, Theorem 16.6 establishes: if
<MATH_0005> is a Deligne-Mumford stack finite type over a Noetherian scheme,
then
there exists a finite, surjective, generically <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism <MATH_0006>
with <MATH_0007> a scheme. It is also shown in Corollary 16.6.2 that any Noetherian
normal algebraic space is isomorphic to the algebraic space quotient <MATH_0008>
for a finite group <MATH_0009> acting a normal scheme <MATH_0010>.
<STRUCT_0008>
<STRUCT_0009> Edidin, Hassett, Kresch, Vistoli:
<EMPHOPEN_0003>Brauer Groups and Quotient stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0003> <REF_0004>
<STRUCT_0010>
Theorem 2.7 states:
if <MATH_0011> is an algebraic stack of finite type over a
Noetherian ground scheme <MATH_0012>, then the diagonal
<MATH_0013> is
quasi-finite if and only if there exists a finite surjective
morphism <MATH_0014> from a scheme <MATH_0015>.
<STRUCT_0011>
<STRUCT_0012> Kresch, Vistoli: <EMPHOPEN_0004>On coverings of Deligne-Mumford stacks and
surjectivity of the Brauer map<EMPHCLOSE_0004> <REF_0005>
<STRUCT_0013>
It is proved here that any smooth, separated Deligne-Mumford stack finite type
over a field with quasi-projective coarse moduli space admits a finite, flat
cover by a smooth quasi-projective scheme.
<STRUCT_0014>
<STRUCT_0015> Olsson: <EMPHOPEN_0005>On proper coverings of Artin stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0005> <REF_0006>
<STRUCT_0016>
Proves that if <MATH_0016> is an Artin stack separated
and finite type over <MATH_0017>, then
there exists a proper surjective morphism <MATH_0018> from a scheme <MATH_0019>
quasi-projective over <MATH_0020>. As an application, Olsson proves coherence and
constructibility of direct image sheaves under proper morphisms. As an
application, he proves Grothendieck's existence theorem for proper
Artin stacks.
<STRUCT_0017>
<STRUCT_0018> Rydh: <EMPHOPEN_0006>Noetherian approximation of algebraic spaces and stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0006>
<REF_0007>
<STRUCT_0019>
Theorem B of this paper is as follows.
Let <MATH_0021> be a quasi-compact algebraic stack with quasi-finite and separated
diagonal (resp.<SPACE_0001>a quasi-compact Deligne-Mumford stack
with quasi-compact and separated diagonal). Then there exists a scheme
<MATH_0022> and a finite, finitely presented and surjective morphism <MATH_0023>
that is flat (resp.<SPACE_0002><ACCENT_0002>tale) over a dense quasi-compact open substack
<MATH_0024>.
<STRUCT_0020>
